GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: build_machine (cultists.py:24-34) vs GenerateMoveStateMachine (CalcifiedCultist.cs:66-75). Node-for-node identical, executed with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py graphs`: INCANTATION_MOVE (BuffIntent -> Intent(BUFF)) -> DARK_STRIKE_MOVE (SingleAttackIntent(9) -> Intent(ATTACK, damage=9)) -> itself; initial state INCANTATION_MOVE; states list [INCANTATION, DARK_STRIKE] in the same order. No RandomBranchState and no ConditionalBranchState on either side, so PROMPT.md bug class 6 (AddBranch integer arguments) cannot apply and no move roll ever draws. By monster_state_machine step 28 both machines start with a one-entry StateLog ([INCANTATION_MOVE], executed) because the initial state is a loggable MoveState, and by step 30 the first roll is the sticky no-op.

Sim cultists.py:39 PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, self, RitualPower, self.incantation_amt, applier=self). Same target, same applier, same amount, no card on either side. The PlayerChoiceContext argument is multiplayer-only (PROMPT.md scope) and is not a divergence.

Sim cultists.py:42 self._execute_attack(ctx, self.dark_strike_dmg, 1) hits ctx.player once (monsters/base.py:107-118). The Ironclad-only sim has exactly one player, so the target sets coincide.
